name: Brawler
description:
You see the blow coming and move your head just in time so that the guard's fist smashes into the face of the soldier restraining you. You feel the grip loosen on your arms and you break free, jabbing an elbow behind you and rolling to your feet two paces away. You survey the chairs around the tavern table, choose the sturdiest-looking one, and raise it above your head with a shout, charging back toward the guard. At the last moment you pivot, swinging it instead at the soldier, who is knocked to the ground as the chair shatters around them. The guard raises their sword to strike you, but suddenly you dive for their legs. Why? Because your friend is coming at them from behind with a tackle, and knees are more likely to break if you brace them against the direction of the blow. A smile spreads across your face as you anticipate the impact, already formulating how you'll tell the tale at the pub tonight or - if things don't go well - to the other inmates.

Brawlers love a good fight - the messier the better. Blows given and blows taken are all part of the fun. Of course, any hot-tempered brute could take joy in violence, but you've elevated it to an art. What might look like chaos to an outsider is actually an intricate dance of anticipation, reaction, clever maneuvering and - when you're having a good day - a healthy sense of humor. Those brave enough to fight alongside you will find that their own attacks land more often and harder the wilder things get.

The Brawler mestiere uses the chaos of a battle as a resource. With the Embrace The Chaos ability, you accumulate MP as violence erupts around you, and you may spend it to empower your own attacks or the attacks of the allies at your back. You're the best in the game at fighting unarmed and with improvised objects, and you get two attacks per turn from day one. All this comes with some challenging personality quirks that are part and parcel to the discipline: impatience, a short temper and a Mistrust of Magic which drives you to break things. You are untrained in any weapons or armor: your best defense is offense.

Brawler is a mestiere that will have you out in front but keeping a level head even as you take hits. It rewards recklessness and combative creativity, but also requires tactical thinking and teamwork.

Play a Brawler if you want to:

  • Thrive in the thick of it, drawing power from chaos and violence and helping your friends make the most of the mayhem.

  • Fight with your fists and whatever's near at hand, treating weapons and spells as unnecessary ornament to a good, straight-ahead fight.

  • Get hit, keep going, and hit back harder, turning your own desperation into a source of power as things get rough.

Questions to consider when making a Brawler:

  • Where did they learn—or develop—their fighting style? A rough upbringing? Tavern brawls? A pit-fighting circuit? Training in a punishing martial discipline?

  • How do they feel about their impatience? Is it something they've accepted, something they're working on, or something they actively lean into as a statement about how the world works?

  • Do they have a code—rules about who they fight, how hard, and when they stop—or do they decide each time from scratch?

  • What's their relationship with magic? Wary suspicion, outright contempt, fearful avoidance, or a conviction that you can't trust anything you can't punch?

  • What's the fight that made them who they are? Did they win it?

novizio.description: You have extensive experience defending yourself with your bare hands, and have been known to pick a fight now and then. You have made some clever observations about how to "read" a fight, which sets you apart.
novizio.baseMpNotes: You gain MP with your Embrace the Chaos ability.
novizio.abilities: Action Over Deliberation, Embrace The Chaos, Fists Up
novizio.gratuiti: Your favorite "fighting clothes," a roll of hand wrap, a small token you always touch for good luck before a fight.
